The bound is kept through every change that lowers the capacity — S11's operator, a new `builtBand`, a carry that shrinks the wings, a moved face of a spanned passage, a change of heights or class, an edit of a table the function reads or of the band set — by re-homing the households past it, the last in address order, by §4.7's overflow pass inside the causing event, never by refusing the change, because refusing would make an ordinary edit fail on a count the user never set, while re-homing is exactly what the generation fill already does with a household its shell cannot hold (repair round 3: V-MAB2-01). swaps.old_row: | J-A28.26 | Chose the canonical chain as the re-cut's definition — the plan for a band row and a household count derived from the as-built plan by least-disruption steps in one fixed order, the rows first (one band at a time, the count clamped into each row's range) and then the households (one at a time) — with what stays stated once in the forms the kernel's transient arena takes (the shell — each storey's seed rings: the wings' extents clipped to tile, the span ring at the ground storey, the basement ring below it — opened again unchanged as the arena's seeds; the entrances and the hearths as anchors placed before any cut; the stair core's bay, the chimney stacks, the passage room, the composer's rooms and the kept rooms as `fixed` rings), the kept-room rule read on the seed ring the room lies in as the arena clips it, and a stored plan re-cut inside its changing event with the shell's identity across it read on rings stripped of the `composition`-role vertices its new walls add, over the cached result at click time or households-first, over a fixed list that passed seeds and vertices as `fixed` rings, and over a kept-room rule read on the wing's unclipped ring, because a chain from committed state makes the plan a function of its inputs alone (§6.2, §6.5 (9)) and returns the as-built plan exactly when the households are re-united; rows first lets each household step happen with the final unit form, so the interior degrades before it multiplies, which is cheaper and what real subdivision did; a wing ring or a basement ring passed as a `fixed` ring would be one uncut face and an entrance is a vertex, not a ring (§3.4's contract); after item 18 changes an earlier overlapping wing a later wing's clipped seed moves although its ring does not, so a room kept by its wing ring would be refused by the arena (`overlap`); and J-P48 (1) makes every new wall end on an exterior wall a footprint vertex in the same event — a split that moves nothing — so the shell's byte-identity bars read the shell without those vertices, as §7.3 item 7 (ii) does (§2.6; item 28 (f); with J-A28.71 amended and the kernel's J-A28.33; repair round 2: V-MAB1-06, V-MAB1-08, V-MAB1-09, VK1-03). A wing whose extent at a storey lies wholly inside another's is clipped after that container (two identical extents keep wing order), so it has no piece there — its floor is the container's — and no piece has a hole, which §3.4's seed clip refuses, because a seed is one ring; and since the one overlay puts every crossing vertex on the earlier ring too, a change of an overlapping wing re-cuts the rooms of the wing before it as well as after it (repair round 3: V-MAB2-09 with VK2-05 and VD2-09). A composed tower stands in the clip order before every wing it engages, over taking it last with its room clipped to a partial disk, because a round tower keeps its round room (the realism tiebreaker; a composer's towers are whole) and the engaged wing's rooms take the arc as a wall; every other composer's room lies inside its own wing's piece, so every fixed ring lies inside one seed (verify-kernel-r3 VK3-01; closing ruling). The composed towers take one of two places in the clip order — before all the wings, in `Composition.towers` order, or, for a tower wholly inside a wing that overlaps no wing taken before that container, directly after its container — and no tower lies wholly inside another, over ordering a tower before each wing it engages and after each wing that contains it, which gives no order for two engaged towers or for a tower inside one wing that engages an earlier wing, and over clipping such a tower's round room to its container's piece, because the two places always give one order with no holed piece; a tower that engages a wing taken before its container keeps its whole round room there, since that wing already carries its cut to the container's edge (the realism tiebreaker; a composer's towers are whole); of two engaged towers — a stair turret on a tower — the later in the composer's order takes the earlier's arc; and a tower inside another tower would give two overlapping round rooms, which the arena refuses, or a round room with a hole, while a stair inside a tower is its spiral core (handfix-b verify-model-r0 VHM-04 with verify-kernel-r0 VKH-01, reconciled). |

swaps.old_row: | J-A28.34 | Chose to build a transient arena's input rings as exact topology — a lattice point two rings share one vertex, a side two rings share one edge, a vertex within the hot pixel of another ring's side splitting that side, no attraction — refusing with `E_DEGENERATE` (detail `seed`, `fixed` or `overlap`) a ring that would break `minEdge`, clearance or simplicity and any overlap, which one winding walk finds; to require seed rings that tile, a caller whose wings overlap passing each clipped against the wings before it; and to require each fixed ring inside one seed ring — over inserting the rings as `mandatory` chains under §3.6's attraction, as J-A28.31 first chose, and over accepting overlapping seeds, or fixed rings anywhere in the seeds' union. Attraction would move a kept room on a re-cut: an earlier cut may split a vertex onto a wall 25.29–26 cm from its corner (§3.2 (2)), and re-inserting it would move it onto that corner, so J-A28.33's promise that a kept room re-enters unchanged would fail for a share of rooms; a refusal is typed and caught by F-PLAN (§5.2) where a silent move would change a kept room. Overlapping seeds would count their overlap twice in the tiling check, enclose it in fixed edges no merge may delete (a forced room) and make `readBack`'s seed tags ambiguous; a fixed ring across the joint between two wings would be split by it into two faces, although a fixed ring is a face no cut divides. The construction is a second door for edges beside `insertChain`, confined to a transient arena's opening as §3.9's load is to a stored plat. Every vertex a face partitioner places on a fixed edge is placed against the input sides that edge lies on, as passed — the input sides are the arena's routes, as a plat's coarser route is for the Steiner vertices on it — over placing it against the sub-edge an earlier split left, because on a one-level arena each sub-edge would be its own route, and same-level splits of a rotated side then drift its later vertices beyond the hot pixel of the straight line, where the construction cannot split the side when a kept room re-enters and refuses the room (a model of §3.6's rule: one side in nine split four times, worst 1.6 cm, `docs/validation/bench/amendb_verify_kernel_r1_drift.out`; placed against the input side, no vertex beyond the hot pixel, no failed search and no refused kept corner over 400 000 splits, `docs/validation/bench/amendb_repair_kernel_r2_routes.out`). The input side is the route that placement and the grid read, never the unit of an answer: a query and `readBack` return and key every edge on its own endpoints, over keying a fixed edge by the input side it lies on, because one side carries every wall segment that ends on it and an edge can lie on two to four input sides, so a key read on the side would tie those segments and have no one value for such an edge, while an edge's own endpoints — every vertex of a one-level arena being of its level — give §3.3's total key. Overlapping wings are clipped as the faces of one overlay of the storey's rings, each face going to the first ring in the caller's clip order that contains it (`tileRings`), over one `booleans('difference', …)` per ring, because separate overlays leave an earlier ring without the crossing vertices a later one gains and can place a T's second crossing off the bar's straight side (1.3 % of cases, worst 1.06 cm), refusing a valid building's seeds; one overlay gives every ring each crossing vertex, so the joints are shared vertex for vertex. A piece left with a hole — an earlier wing wholly inside a later one — is refused, because a seed is one ring; the plan rung's clip order puts a contained wing after its container, which takes the enclosed rooms (§2.6), so the refusal marks a bug. It amends J-A28.31's insertion and J-A28.33's claim that a kept room reads back byte-identical: a new wall ending on a kept room adds a vertex within the hot pixel of its side, so the room keeps its polygon — its vertices unmoved and in order — rather than its bytes (§3.4, §3.10; items 28, 28 (f); repair-kernel-r1 after verify-kernel-r0's VK-02 and VK-03; amended by repair-kernel-r2 after verify-kernel-r1's VK1-01 and VK1-10, and by repair-kernel-r3 after validate's VK2-01 and VK2-04). |
